chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who does not have water with him, while water is to the right and left of the road at a distance of two ghālwahs or about that. He said: “I do not command him to expose himself to danger, lest a thief or a beast confront him.”
And this report indicates that whenever he does not fear a thief or a beast, seeking it becomes obligatory upon him, even if it is at the distance of two ghālwahs.

key_terms.الطَّلَبُ: the act of searching for water before resorting to tayammum
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report used as evidence for the legal ruling
key_terms.غَلْوَتَيْنِ: a measured distance of two arrow-shots, indicating a limited search range
key_terms.لِصٌّ: a thief whose presence creates fear and hardship
key_terms.يُغَرِّرَ بِنَفْسِهِ: to place himself in danger or at serious risk

ai.seo_question: Must a person search for water before performing tayammum if the water is nearby but the الطريق may be dangerous?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of seeking water before resorting to tayammum when water is nearby. It indicates that one must search for water within a moderate distance unless doing so would expose him to danger such as a thief or a predatory animal.
